title: Why a 28% Rally Target Is Actually Ordinary
speaker: Ed Yardeni (views relayed by tastylive host, Options Math Check)

macro_themes.view: The 10-year briefly topping 5% prompted Yardeni to trim his year-end S&P target and raise bear-case odds to 30%.
10,000 by end-2029 is only ~8% a year, close to the index's ordinary historical return and within options-implied ranges.

calls.reason: Yardeni cut his year-end target from 8,400 to 7,900 after the 10y hit 5% and raised bear odds to 30%, but kept 10,000 by end-2029; host says options pricing makes this ordinary.
calls.quote: He cut his year-end S&P 500 target from 8400 to 7900... but 10,000 by the end of 2029 didn't change

notes: Medium-term target 7,900 is a year-end 2026 target (~1% above 7,800), so bias recorded neutral. Long-term target is end-2029. These are Yardeni's views relayed by the host, not an in-video interview.
